rapanui_nuahine: The old woman in the moon (the Rapa Nui Hina), a lunar figure with no attested kin in the island tradition — Routledge (1919); Métraux, Ethnology of Easter Island (1940).
tahitian_maui: The Society-Islands Māui (priest and sun-snarer, later deified) has a famous pan-Polynesian genealogy, but none of his Tahitian kin is separately registered, so he is authored without a within-batch edge — Ellis, Polynesian Researches (1829); Henry, Ancient Tahiti (1928).
tahitian_ruahatu: The ocean-god of the Ra'iātea deluge is given no parent, consort, or sibling in the sources — only his ocean-deep and the fishermen who wake him to the flood — Henry, Ancient Tahiti (1928); Ellis, Polynesian Researches (1829).
tongan_seketoa: The deified shark-god of Niuatoputapu with a continuous local cult; he belongs to the Maʻatu/Niuatoputapu line (none authored here), and the one tradition tying him to the main Tuʻi Tonga line is weakly attested, so no in-batch kin edge is asserted — Gifford, Tongan Myths and Tales (1924); Collocott (1928).
mangaian_ina: Gill fixes no divine parentage, spouse, or sibling for Ina/Ina-moe-aitu within the cosmogonic genealogy (the Tuna-eel tale supplies only her god-lover Tuna, not authored) — Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), Ch. V.
mangaian_maui: The Mangaian Maui's parents (Ru, Buataranga) and elder brothers are named by Gill but not authored in this batch, so no within-batch kin edge is wired — Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), Ch. III.
mangaian_miru: Gill gives Miru (Miru-kura) of Avaiki, who cooks the souls of the dead, no parent, spouse, or sibling — only her daughters the Tapairu (not authored) — Gill, Myths and Songs from the South Pacific (1876), Ch. IX.
marquesan_tu: Named among the great Marquesan atua (Handy, Native Culture of the Marquesas, 1923, p. 247) but without a fixed genealogy linking Tu to the other figures; kin omitted rather than invented.
marquesan_pohu: Legendary hero named among the foremost Marquesan narrative figures (Handy 1923, p. 247; Marquesan Legends 1930) with no attested genealogical link to the batch figures.
marquesan_akaui: Legendary character named among the foremost Marquesan narrative figures (Handy 1923, p. 247; Marquesan Legends 1930) with no attested kin.
ewe_da: The rainbow-serpent Aido-Hwedo / Anyi-eʋo, a pre-existent serpent who upholds the world coiled in the sea — not begotten of Mawu-Lisa; no parentage attested — Ellis, The Ewe-Speaking Peoples (1890); Herskovits, Dahomey (1938).
ewe_afa: The vodu of divination and destiny (the Fa/Ifa oracle); no consistent begotten parentage in the tradition — Parrinder, West African Religion (1961); Herskovits, Dahomey (1938).
ewe_avlekete: The sea/lagoon-shore vodu whose parentage varies by source (Agbe/Naete or Sogbo, neither authored), so left unwired — Herskovits, Dahomey (1938).
tuamotuan_kiho: Kiho-tumu, the self-existent Source of Stimson's esoteric Tuamotuan recension, kept distinct from the standard Atea-Fakahotu cosmogony and left unharmonized; no kin attested — Stimson, The Cult of Kiho-tumu (1933); Emory, Tuamotuan Concepts of Creation (JPS 49, 1940).
tuamotuan_tahaki: The red-skinned hero Tahaki (Tafaki); his thin name-level kin (Hema, Karihi) are not authored, so no within-batch kin edge is wired — Stimson, Legends of Maui and Tahaki (1934).
tuamotuan_puna: The shark-form king of Hiti-marama in the Rata/Vahi-vero cycle, with no attested divine kin among the batch figures — Stimson, Tuamotuan Legends (1937); Emory.
purepecha_auicanime: The goddess of hunger/famine, attested as an independent force (the deceiving-old-woman famine myth) with no genealogy, consort, or kin — Relación de Michoacán (c. 1540).
zapotec_pitao_xoo: The earthquake-god (the deified tremor, xoo), attested purely as a functional force with no genealogy, consort, or kin — Córdova, Vocabulario (1578); Sellen, El cielo compartido (2007).
zapotec_pitao_peeze: The god of omens/fate, with no genealogy or consort recorded; the only tie is Pitao Xicala (dreams) reckoned an aspect of him, wired on Xicala — Lind, Ancient Zapotec Religion (2015); Whitecotton (1977).
zulu_umamlambo: Zulu/Nguni river-divinity and shape-shifting serpent of fortune (uMamlambo, "Mother of the River"); attested as a free-standing nature-spirit and diviners’ familiar with no parentage or kin in Callaway (1868–70) or Berglund (1976).
zulu_inkanyamba: Zulu/Xhosa storm-and-tornado river-serpent of Howick Falls (iNkanyamba, "Lord of the Waters"); a lone serpent-being with no attested genealogy or kin — the lore-motif of seeking a mate is not a registry kin-relation (Berglund 1976).
kyrgyz_er_toshtuk: Hero of a self-standing Kyrgyz epic (Er Töshtük) only loosely attached to the Manas orbit; his canonical kin (father Eleman, wife Kenjeke, the seven brothers) are not registered here, leaving no same-tradition kinship to anchor.
kyrgyz_kojojash: Hunter-hero of the archaic standalone Kyrgyz small-epic Kojojash; his antagonist is the supernatural grey she-goat Sur-Echki rather than any human kin, and no in-registry relatives exist to anchor an edge.
sogdian_zurvan: Sogdian personification of infinite Time and Destiny (Zurvan/Azruwa), a cosmic abstraction at the head of the high triad with no individuated in-registry kin.
bactrian_mao: Kushan moon-god of the imperial coinage; a titular dynastic deity attested numismatically with no genealogy or in-registry kin.
bactrian_pharro: Deified royal Glory (Khwarenah) on the Kushan coins — a hypostatized abstraction of God-given kingship rather than a figure with kin.
bactrian_ardoxsho: Deified Abundance (Aši) on the Kushan coins, the cornucopia-goddess of reward; a hypostatized power with no in-registry kinship.
bactrian_oaxsho: Divine personification of the Oxus river (Wakhsh) venerated at Takht-i Sangin; a local river-god with no registered kin.
turkic_yer_sub: The composite Holy Earth-Water (ıduq Yer-Sub) of the Orkhon inscriptions — a primordial land-and-water power ranked below Tengri, with no individuated kin in the registry.
turkic_yayik: A celestial messenger-spirit (numen) of the Altai sacrificial cosmology who serves the creator Ülgen; a functional intermediary with no kinship of his own recorded here.
turkic_korkut_ata: Legendary Oghuz/Kazakh shaman-bard of the Syr Darya; a standalone culture-hero whose canonical kin are not registered, leaving no in-tradition edge to anchor.
yakut_ayisit: Sakha birth-goddess who brings the soul to the newborn; a functional power of childbirth with no individuated kin in the registry.
yakut_uluu_toyon: Sakha thunder-and-fire lord of the upper world, master of the abaasy; a cosmic power authored without registered kinship (distinct from, not kin to, Ürüng Aiyy Toyon).
kalenjin_asis: Kalenjin supreme sun/sky god (Asis < Asista, "the sun"); in Hollis, The Nandi (1909) he stands beside the thunder-being Ilet as the two principal divinities, but no genealogical kin is attested, leaving no same-tradition kinship to anchor.
kalenjin_chemosit: Kalenjin folklore ogre — the one-legged half-man child-devourer of Nandi tale (Hollis 1909); a free-standing bogey with no attested parentage, consort or offspring.
luba_kabezya_mpungu: Luba self-existent creator high god (Mvidi Mukulu / Shakapanga) who withdraws after creation; the genesis cycle attests no individuated divine kin for him (de Heusch, The Drunken King 1982; Womersley 1984).
mbuti_khonvoum: Mbuti sky-creator and great hunter of the Ituri; Schebesta and Turnbull attest his deeds (the serpent-rainbow bow, the tri-coloured clay creation) but no divine genealogy, leaving him kinless in the registry.
mbuti_negoogunogumbar: Mbuti forest ogre — a thinly-attested child-eating giant of Ituri tale (Turnbull 1961); recorded as a free-standing monster with no attested kin.
tumbuka_chikangombe: Tumbuka python sky-divinity of the highlands; his bond to the high god Chiuta is cult mediation rather than kinship and his spirit-wives are dedicated human women, so no divine kin edge is attested (T. Cullen Young 1932).
tumbuka_chiuta: Tumbuka self-existent creator and rainbow/rain god ("the great bow"); a self-originating high god with no attested divine parentage, consort or offspring (T. Cullen Young 1932).
punic_astarte: Inherited Phoenician goddess (Ashtart) present in Punic cult; her canonical consorts and kin belong to the eastern Phoenician homeland pantheon rather than the Carthaginian batch, so no in-tradition kinship is attested here (Lancel, Carthage 1995; Lipiński 1995).
punic_baal_shamem: Carthaginian sky-god "Lord of the Heavens," invoked in the Hannibal–Philip V state oath (Polybius 7.9); named in the cult formulae without any attested genealogy, consort or offspring in the Punic evidence.
punic_eshmun: Punic healer god of the great Byrsa temple at Carthage (interpretatio Asklepios); his consort and kin are not attested within the authored Carthaginian pantheon, leaving no in-tradition kinship to anchor (Lancel, Carthage 1995).
punic_resheph: West Semitic plague-and-war god whose Carthaginian cult is itself uncertain (Xella); attested in the western Mediterranean without a local Punic genealogy, consort or offspring.
mandaean_hayyi_rabbi: As the uncreated, wholly transcendent supreme God of Mandaeism, the Great Life has no parents and no peers; the lower Lives and uthras are emanated subordinates that depend on him, so he stands at the apex of the hierarchy without a reciprocal kin or peer bond (Drower 1937; Rudolph, Encyclopaedia Iranica).
chumash_momoy: Momoy stands alone among the named Chumash sky and earth powers because she belongs to the cycle of the First People as the personified datura plant rather than to the genealogy of the upper-world or creation deities, and no spouse, sibling, or parent is attested for her in the recorded narratives.
palmyrene_baalshamin: Baalshamin was an independent supreme sky-god heading his own sanctuary and his own triad (with Aglibol and Malakbel), parallel to but cultically distinct from Bel rather than paired with the other named figures.
palmyrene_allat: Allat was a distinct pre-Islamic Arabian goddess with her own temple in the western quarter, assimilated to Athena and not incorporated into either of Palmyra's two great divine triads.
yolngu_laindjung: Laindjung stands alone here because his attested kin and counterparts in the Yirritja tradition (Barama, Banaidja and the brother Garaginya) are not authored as separate figures in this set, leaving him without a reciprocated relationship inside it.
shuar_tsunki: Tsunki is attested as the singular primordial water-spirit and 'first shaman', the diffuse origin of all shamanic power rather than a being embedded in a divine family, and no spouse, sibling, or parent is recorded for it in the ethnographic sources (Harner 1972; Perruchon 2003).
shuar_arutam: Arútam is attested not as a personal deity within a genealogy but as an ancient, diffuse ancestral vision-power passing through successive human holders at the sacred waterfalls, and the sources record no kin, spouse, or peer relations for it (Harner 1972; Rubenstein 2002).
choctaw_hashtahli: Hashtahli is the sun regarded as the all-seeing supreme overseer; the ethnographic sources name his associated stars and moon but attest no parent, sibling, or spouse among the other individuated beings in this set.
choctaw_nanih_waiya: Nanih Waiya is the sacred origin-mound itself, the venerated mother-place from which the people emerge; it is a numinous landscape locus and the sources give it no genealogical kin or peer-relations among the other figures here.
lobi_kotin: The accomplished ancestor is an individuated deified human raised by completed funerary ritual and venerated within his own household's sacred chamber, and so stands apart from the genealogy of created spirits that descends from the sky-god through the thila and bush spirits.
yazidi_tawusi_melek: As the supreme chief of the Heptad and viceroy of the one God, the Peacock Angel stands at the apex of the Yezidi divine order, with the other Holy Beings ranked beneath him rather than beside him as kin (Allison, Encyclopaedia Iranica, 2004).
bugis_sawerigading: Within this core divine set he stands alone because his nearest kin in the epic — his father Batara Lattuq, his twin sister We Tenriabeng, and his wife We Cudai — fall outside the five apical figures authored here; his link to the set is genealogical descent from Batara Guru rather than a wired spousal or sibling tie (Koolhof 1999; Pelras 1996).
arrernte_altyerre: Altyerre stands apart as an eternal, uncreated sky high-god whose theological standing is debated; he is not given kin or a creation-partner among the Arrernte beings, and Carl Strehlow recorded him as a being who had no beginning rather than as a relative of the other ancestors.
tiwi_mudungkala: Mudungkala is the primordial creator of Tiwi cosmology.
murinbata_mutjingga: The Old Woman / Mother of the Karwadi (Punj) bullroarer rite stands apart from the Kunmanggur cycle; Stanner records no kin tie binding her to the other named Murinbata beings, her swallowing myth being self-contained.
murinbata_kukpi: The Black-Snake Woman is an independent travelling ancestress with her own myth of springs and destruction at Purgala, and Stanner attests no genealogical link between her and the figures of the Rainbow-Serpent cycle.
kiowa_saynday: Saynday the trickster culture-hero stands outside the genealogy of the Sun and the medicine-twins; Kiowa tradition presents him as a self-existing being with no recorded parents or kin, invariably introduced simply as 'Saynday was coming along' (Mooney 1898; Marriott 1963).
lenape_kishelemukong: As the supreme Creator who made the world and the lesser manitowak by thought and then withdrew, Kishelemukong has no attested parents and stands above, rather than within, the web of kin relations; the lesser spirits are subordinate to him but he answers to none.
lenape_wehixamukes: Wehixamukes is a self-standing human trickster-hero of the Lenape storytelling cycle with no attested parentage or kin among the divine manitowak; the tradition presents him as an isolated comic protagonist rather than a member of the pantheon's genealogy.
klamath_kmukamtch: Stands at the origin of the Klamath cosmos as the primordial old-man creator, with no parents recorded and his kin (the son Aishish, the guise Marten, the Modoc cognate Kumush) all derived from or pointing toward him rather than the reverse.
klamath_coyote: Appears as a self-standing trickster animal-person across the Klamath and Modoc tales with no fixed genealogy or stable kin tie attested in the ethnographic record, recurring independently in many separate narratives.
wayuu_maleiwa: Maleiwa is the solitary creator and culture-hero of the Wayuu: in the ethnographic corpus he is born from his mother's remains and acts alone to order the world and make the Wayuu, without an attested spouse, sibling or genealogical tie to the rain-and-drought couple Juya and Pulowi.
batammariba_oyinkakwata: Oyinkakwata, 'the Rich Man Above,' is attested as an independent sky-and-storm god of the Batammariba with no recorded genealogy or kin tie to the solar Kuiye or the earth goddess Butan (Blier 1987; Mercier 1968).
idoma_owoicho: As the uncreated, self-existent and transcendent Supreme Being who stands above and apart from every other power, Owoicho has no parents and enters into no peer relationship; all other divinities and the ancestors are subordinate to him rather than his kin or equals.
sukuma_liwelelo: The Sukuma creator is a solitary, distant and uncaused being who made the cosmos and then withdrew; the tradition attributes to him no consort, parentage or kin, only the multiple names Liwelelo, Lyuba, Lubangwe and Seba (Cory 1953; Maganda 2002).
sukuma_ngwana_malundi: The legendary elephant-hunter and trickster culture-hero stands alone in the song tradition, with no attested genealogy or fixed kin among the named Sukuma figures, the bayege associations he heads being remembered as of obscure origin (Gunderson 2010, 2008).
illyrian_redon: Redon is attested only as a solitary civic and maritime tutelary deity on coins and dedications, with no recorded consort, parentage or divine kin in the surviving Illyrian epigraphy.
illyrian_medaurus: Medaurus appears only as the lone protective god of Risinium, named in isolation on the Lambaesis dedication and local cult, with no attested genealogy or companion deities.
illyrian_anzotica: Anzotica is documented as a self-standing Liburnian goddess at Aenona, the indigenous deities of the Liburni being almost exclusively independent local goddesses without recorded divine family ties.
illyrian_bindus: Bindus is attested solely as the water-god of the Iapodes at the Privilica spring, with no consort, parent or sibling named in the votive record.
albanian_folk_pantheon_zojz: Zojz stands alone at the apex of the Albanian pantheon as the supreme sky-and-lightning father, attested without a fixed divine consort in the folk record though named as the father of the dawn goddess Prende (Elsie 2001; Mallory & Adams 1997).
chuvash_hert_surt: Hĕrt-surt is a self-contained household hearth-spirit attached to the individual dwelling and its family, with no attested genealogy or named relationship to the other deities of the Chuvash pantheon.
naxi_igu_ake: Igu Ake is conceived as an abstract first cause preceding the manifest pantheon, attested as the primordial origin from which the gods proceed rather than through any attested kinship, marriage, or partnership among the named figures.
naxi_heduwapa: Heduwapa, the god of White Bones, is attested only as a name and rank within the supreme triad of the Dongba pantheon, with no recorded marriage, descent, or symmetric bond to another individuated figure in the Naxi sources.
yi_ngeti_gunzy: As the primordial sky god and head of the celestial palace, Ngeti Gunzy stands at the apex of the cosmic genealogy with no parents of his own recorded in the Book of Origins.
yi_zhyge_alu: Zhyge Alu is born not of a divine couple but from drops of eagle and dragon-eagle blood that fall upon the mortal weaver Pumo Hniyyr, and is reared apart by dragons, so he stands outside the marriage-and-descent network of the other figures.
toda_kwoten: Kwoten is a deified culture-hero whose recorded legends center on his own exploits and on his vanishing after union with an un-individuated female deity, so no named partner or kin within this set is securely attested.
toda_notirzi: Notirzi is preserved only as a divine name invoked in Toda dairy-prayers beside Teikirzi, with no narrative establishing kinship or a reciprocal bond to any other named figure in this set.
mizo_pu_vana: As the sky-grandfather and apical elder of the heavenly household, Pu Vana heads the divine genealogy and his own parentage is unattested; his fatherhood of Pathian is recorded on Pathian's lineage (B. Lalthangliana, Culture and Folklore of Mizoram, 2005).
mizo_vanchungnula: Vanchungnula stands apart from the symmetric kin-network as the rain-maiden of Pathian's household, attached to it only as his celestial daughter and otherwise unpartnered in the sources (Billy J. Zorinthara, 'Spirit in Creation', Studies in World Christianity 30.1, 2024).
mizo_lasi: Lasi is a self-standing forest power, the divine owner of wild game, with no attested kinship or marriage to the other named deities of the Mizo pantheon (J. Shakespear, The Lushei Kuki Clans, 1912).
mizo_phung: Phung is an independent malevolent ogress-spirit of the wild, attested without genealogical ties to the benevolent heavenly family (J.H. Lorrain, Dictionary of the Lushai Language, 1940).
tani_pedong_nane: Pedong Nane stands at the head of the Adi creation genealogy as the primordial mother who gives birth to all beings; within this authored set her descent from the creator Sedi and her union with Yidum Bote lie outside the figures recorded here, her direct link being the maternal one to Abotani and the Epom captured through their parentage rather than her own relations.
tani_kine_nane: Kine Nane is the goddess of grain and crops in the religion of the Tani peoples, an earth-and-harvest deity whose blessing secures the fertility of the rice fields.
nias_inada_samadulo_hose: As the unmarried primordial Mother who stands at the very origin of the genealogy, Ina-da Samadulo Höse has no spouse, sibling or peer of her own; the divine couple and brother-pair descend from her rather than standing beside her (Schröder, Nias, 1917; Suzuki, Religious System and Culture of Nias, 1959).
niuean_tagaloa: Tagaloa belongs to the cosmic sky-and-creator stratum that Niue shares with the wider Polynesian world and is not woven into the island-making band of migrating tupua; the early ethnographies record no attested kin or peer relations for him within the Niuean set.
diyari_mura: Although Mura heads the class of mura-mura creators, no genealogy or named kin tie to another individuated figure is attested in the early sources; Gason (1874) presents the Good Spirit as a solitary creative power working through the Moon.
diyari_darana: Darana's legend, as recorded by Siebert and Howitt (1902) and by Reuther, centres on his own deeds of rain and increase and names no attested kin or spouse among the other individuated mura-mura of this set.
diyari_mandramankana: Reuther's notes (Scherer trans. 1981) record Mandramankana's deeds and his return from death as those of a single travelling culture hero, without an attested kin or partnership tie to another figure in this set.
diyari_adnoartina: Adnoartina's one well-attested relationship is his enmity with the dog Marindi, who is not authored as a figure in this set; he has no attested kinship or partnership with another individuated Diyari being recorded here.
igala_ayegba: Ayegba Ọmaidoko enters the set as the historical Ata whose daughter Inikpi names him as her father, so the only attested genealogical link runs toward him from Inikpi and he carries no outgoing relations of his own within this set.
igala_omodoko: Omodoko is remembered only as a self-sacrificing princess of the Igala–Jukun war whose precise parentage and kin are not securely fixed in the tradition, the legend often conflating her with Inikpi; she therefore stands without firmly attested genealogical or relational ties within this set.
iraqw_gii_dead: The Iraqw dead form a collective ancestral category rather than a named individual with attested kin or peer ties to the other deities, and the sources record no genealogy or symmetric relationship linking them personally to Looa or Neetlangw.
manichaean_father_of_greatness: As the uncreated supreme God who stands at the head of the entire emanative hierarchy, the Father of Greatness has no parents and enters into no peer relationship; every other divinity descends from him as a one-directional evocation.
venetic_reitia: No genealogy or divine consort is attested for Reitia in the Venetic inscriptions; she appears as an autonomous tutelary goddess of the Este-Baratella sanctuary, accompanied only by her own epithets Śainati and Pora.
venetic_trumusiatis: Trumusiatis is attested solely as the solitary tutelary god of the Làgole spring-sanctuary; the inscriptions name no kin, spouse or associated deity, and he stands alone until his later identification with Apollo.
venetic_louderai: Louderai is known from a single local Cadore dedication with no attested kinship or partnership to any other Venetic deity, standing alone as a regional cult-figure equated with the Latin Libera.
ryukyuan_tedako: The solar lord Tedako stands above the creation in the Omoro Sōshi as the commanding sun-deity and royal title; he issues orders to the creator pair but no kinship or peer bond is attested for him, so he stands alone in the genealogy.
ryukyuan_kinmamon: Kinmamon is recorded as the supreme deity of the Nirai Kanai otherworld in the Ryūkyū Shintō-ki, but the sources establish no kinship or peer relation linking it to the creator deities, so it stands alone.
sinhala_folk_yakku_kalu_kumara: Kalu Kumara stands alone in the named pantheon as the prince-demon of women's afflictions; his legendary genealogy ties him to a mortal royal house outside the demon set rather than to the other named yakku.
sinhala_folk_yakku_maha_kola_sanniya: Maha Kola Sanniya is set apart as chief and maker of the eighteen disease-demons, the diffuse sanni class he created rather than any individuated peer among the named great yakku.
sinhala_folk_yakku_huniyam: Huniyam occupies a solitary interstitial niche between demon and god as the deity of sorcery, his cult and threshold shrines standing distinct from the cemetery and disease yakku of the pantheon.
tharu_bhuiyan: Bhuiyan is the Tharu earth-deity of the village territory, attached to the open bhuinhar shrine rather than to any attested kinship or marriage within the divine set (Rajaure 1982; McDonaugh 1984).
tharu_goraiya: Goraiya is an ancestral boundary-guardian godling whose cult and pig-offering are recorded without any attested genealogy or spouse among the Tharu deities (Gautam & Thapa-Magar 1994; Crooke 1896).
tharu_mainya: Mainya is named only as one of the paired ancestral guardian-deities (goat-offering) and carries no attested parentage or marriage in the published record (Gautam & Thapa-Magar 1994; McDonaugh 1984).
bukidnon_domalongdong: Although ethnographically grouped with three other cardinal wind-deities, Domalongdong has no attested genealogy or named personal tie to them beyond shared subordination to Magbabaya, which is recorded only as a directed relation.
bukidnon_ibabasag: Ibabasag is attested only as a specialized patroness of pregnant women and agent of Magbabaya, with no recorded kinship or peer relationship to other named figures apart from that directed subordination.
bukidnon_ipamahandi: Ipamahandi is attested only as the divinity of accidents and property serving under Magbabaya, with no recorded genealogy or symmetric tie to other named figures beyond that directed subordination.
bukidnon_tigbas: Tigbas is attested only as the most respected of the lesser deities of good government under Magbabaya, with no recorded kinship or peer relationship to other named figures apart from that directed subordination.
makira_kahausibware: Codrington records Kahausibware as a self-existent female hi'ona (snake creator-spirit) of Bauro with no attested parentage or kin among the other named San Cristoval figona; she belongs to a class of beings who were never human.
makira_ngorieru: Fox records Ngorieru only as the chief of the adaro sea-spirits, with no attested genealogy or named kin linking him to the figona creator-serpents of the island.
kunwinjku_yingarna: As the original, primordial mother Rainbow Serpent who emerged from the sea before all others, Yingarna stands at the head of the genealogy with no parents of her own.
kunwinjku_lumaluma: Lumaluma is an incoming giant whale-ancestor from across the sea who acts alone with his wives and stands outside the genealogy of the other named Kunwinjku ancestors.
kunwinjku_algaihgo: Algaihgo is a self-standing fire-woman among the First People whose sources record no kin or partnered relationship with the other named figures of this set.
kunwinjku_namarrkon: Namarrkon the Lightning Man is an independent sky-being of the storm whose Kunwinjku attestations give him no kin tie to the other named figures of this set.
mixe_poj_ene: Mixe religion is organised as a pluralistic system of discrete domain-deities rather than a married pantheon, and the ethnographic sources record no genealogy or kin-tie linking Thunder to the other named gods (Lipp 1991).
mixe_naaxwiiny: The Earth (Naaxwiiñ) is venerated in her own right as the source of sustenance and wisdom, and no attested myth gives her a spouse, parent, or sibling among the other named Mixe deities (Lipp 1991).
mixe_great_lady_life: Great Lady Life stands alone as the deity of conception, childbirth, and medicine; the sources document her function but record no genealogical relation to the other Mixe gods (Lipp 1991).
mixe_mijku: The Lord of the Underworld Mɨjku is defined by his domain over death, illness, and wealth rather than by kinship, and the ethnographic record supplies no attested family tie to the other named deities (Lipp 1991; Kuroda 1984).
mixe_kondoy: Kondoy's mythic sibling is his unnamed brother the serpent of Zempoaltepetl, who is not an individuated named figure, so the hero-king stands alone among the named beings of this set (Miller 1956; Braakhuis and Hull 2014).
warao_kanobo: Kanobo, 'our grandfather', is the supreme being who stands at the apex of the Warao cosmos above its pantheon; the cardinal world-quarter gods are subordinate to him, but he has no attested spouse, sibling, or parent within the tradition.
wichi_ahat: Ahát stands apart as the demonic antithesis of human vitality, governing the spirit-owners hierarchically rather than through any kinship or partnership with the other named beings of the cycle.
embera_antumia: Although bound to the order of the jai, Antumiá is described not as the kin or peer of the high gods but as a solitary, shape-shifting water-being that haunts the rivers alone and answers only to whatever jaibaná has mastered it.
ekoi_obasinjom: Obasinjom is a divinatory medicine-spirit embodied in a mask and disseminated by purchase between communities rather than by descent; Ekoi tradition records no parentage, spouse or kin for it, so it stands alone in the genealogy (Röschenthaler 2004).
ful_e_pastoral_initiatory_tradition_geno: Geno is the remote and uncreated supreme creator who has no genealogy and stands above the pantheon, acting only indirectly through the serpent Tyanaba.
ful_e_pastoral_initiatory_tradition_kaid: Kaïdara is the self-subsisting god of gold and esoteric knowledge of his own initiatory récit, set apart in a subterranean realm and given no kin or consort in the tradition.
mongo_nzakomba: As the transcendent creator high god of the Mongo, Njakomba stands above and apart from the genealogy of the epic ancestors, framing rather than entering their kinship; he is invoked alone under the title Bomongo, 'the Owner' (Korse 2010; Hulstaert 1961).
makonde_nnungu: Nnungu is the remote, transcendent Supreme Being who stands above the genealogies of the ancestral dead and is reached only indirectly through the mahoka, so he is attested without spouse, parentage or kin in the Makonde sources.
eblaite_hadabal: Hadabal headed a regional cult of his own in the Orontes valley (centres at Larugadu and Luban) with only an unnamed female counterpart ('his lady', Belatu) attested, so no individuated kin or peer within this set.
eblaite_kamish: Kamish is documented at Ebla through sacrifices, a sanctuary and a calendar month, but the archive records no spouse, parent or divine peer for him, so he stands alone in this set.
eblaite_ishara: Ishara appears at Ebla as an independent tutelary goddess of the royal family with no consort, parent or sibling named in the Eblaite corpus, and so has no relations within this set.
dilmun_ninsikila: She is known only from the Sumerian Dilmun myths as the consort of Enki (a Mesopotamian god outside the Dilmun set), and although scholars connect her with the goddess Meskilak by name, the texts assign her no kin or social tie to the other named Dilmun figures, so she stands alone.
messapian_damatura: An indigenous earth-mother attested chiefly through her name and its etymology; no genealogy or relationship to another Messapic figure is preserved in the inscriptions, and her links to Greek Demeter are cross-cultural rather than internal to the Messapian set (West 2007, p. 176).
messapian_aprodita: Known from votive dedications such as the Ceglie Messapica stele; no parentage or attested relationship to any other Messapian deity survives, her identification with Aphrodite being a cross-cultural correspondence rather than a Messapic kinship (de Simone & Marchesini 2002).
messapian_thana: A securely attested theonym occurring on Messapic and Dalmatian dedications, but with no preserved myth, genealogy, or relationship to any other figure of the Messapian pantheon (de Simone & Marchesini 2002).
sicel_hybla: Hybla is attested only as the solitary tutelary earth-goddess of the Hyblaean towns, with no genealogy or consort linking her to the Etna-and-geyser cluster of Sikel deities (Pausanias 5.23.6; Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Geography, 1854).
continental_germanic_nerthus: Tacitus names no kin or consort for Nerthus; she is worshipped collectively by seven tribes but stands alone in the attested record, with her relationship to the later Norse Njǫrðr a matter of modern reconstruction rather than ancient genealogy.
continental_germanic_tamfana: Tamfana is attested only by the single notice of her temple's destruction in Tacitus, Annals 1.51, with no recorded family, partner or associated deity.
continental_germanic_baduhenna: Baduhenna is known solely from her sacred grove in Tacitus, Annals 4.73, and no genealogy, consort or companion deity is preserved for her.
continental_germanic_nehalennia: Despite roughly 160 votive altars, Nehalennia is never linked epigraphically to any other named deity, kin or consort, and so stands alone within this set.
nganasan_deiba_nguo: Deiba-nguo, the orphan creator culture-hero, stands apart from the female 'mothers of the world' in Nganasan cosmology and is not given a fixed genealogical bond to them in the attested tales (Gracheva 1983; Dolgikh 1976).
yukaghir_pon: Pon is the diffuse supreme being on the firmament, conceived as standing alone above and apart from the personified master-spirits rather than entering kinship or partnership with them (Jochelson 1926).
zhuang_gyaj: Gyaj the thunder god stands as one of the three complementary cosmic rulers (heaven, water, earth) rather than through any attested kinship or marriage tie in the Zhuang sources.
zhuang_ngweg: Ngweg the dragon king is defined by his rule of the watery realm among the three cosmic rulers, with no attested genealogical or marital relation recorded in the Zhuang scriptures.
zhuang_mehnangz: The Flower Mother Mehnangz is venerated as an independent fertility goddess of the flower garden; her links to Baeuqloxdoh and Moloxgyap are contested and unfixed in the scholarship, so she stands alone.
bai_duan_chicheng: He stands alone in this set as a self-made hero benzhu, deified solely for his python-slaying death at the Erhe River, with no spouse, parentage, or kin attested among the other Bai figures.
bunun_dihanin: Dihanin, the abstract sky-power, stands apart from the figures of myth: it is the encompassing supreme force overseeing all, with no attested genealogy or personal relationships (Joby 2024).
bunun_vali_sun: Vali, the scorching sun, has no attested kin or peers of its own; it is acted upon in the myth - shot and transformed - rather than bound by reciprocal ties (Yushan National Park; H. Hong 2025).
bunun_buan_moon: Buan, the moon, originates as the transformed sun rather than from any parentage, and its mythic dealings with the ancestor are recorded only as that hunter's directed obligation to it (H. Hong 2025; Yushan National Park).
oraon_dharmes: As the one supreme creator and moral arbiter of the cosmos, Dharmes stands at the apex of the Oraon pantheon; the sun, moon and earth are his subordinate representative powers rather than his kin, and he is invoked alone as the high god.
oraon_sarna_burhi: Sarna Burhi belongs to the localized cult of the sacred grove and the village deities rather than to the celestial complex of the supreme god, and is venerated in her own right as the autonomous 'old lady of the grove' without an attested genealogy.
bontoc_kabunian: Recorded as the remote sky high-god and father of Lumawig, Kabunian stands above the genealogy as an originating figure with no attested spouse or sibling of his own within the corpus (Jenks 1905).
tokelauan_fakafotu: Tokelauan storm-and-hurricane god worshipped with his own coral slab at Atafu and a separate god-house at Fakaofo; Macgregor records no kinship tie of any allowed kind to Tui Tokelau, Te Moana, or the other Tokelau gods.
tokelauan_fafie: Deified high chief of Fakaofo and tutelary god of the Sulu clan; though he is set beside Tui Tokelau in cult and figures in the wrestling-match tradition with Leua (who is not in this registry), no attested marriage, sibling, or descent bond links him to another registered Tokelau figure.
tokelauan_mafola: A Tokelau nature-god of the sea known only as a reliably answering power; Macgregor records no genealogy or kinship of any allowed kind connecting him to the other Tokelau gods.
tokelauan_toikia: Strongest of the Tokelau minor gods, remembered only for his role in the Fafie-Leua wrestling match; the source preserves no marriage, sibling, or descent bond of the allowed kinds to other registered Tokelau figures.
tokelauan_tonuailangi: Tokelau god dwelling beyond the horizon, remembered solely for prophecy; Macgregor preserves no kinship of any allowed kind linking him to the other Tokelau gods.
bribri_cabecar_iriria: Iriria stands apart with no symmetric peers: she is brought into being solely as the daughter of Sulá so that her body may become the earth, and is connected to the pantheon only through that directed parentage.
kogi_gauteovan: As the unborn and eternal Great Mother who 'existed first', she has no parents and stands at the apex of creation as its uncaused source, prior to all the lords and ancestors she brings forth.
kogi_aluna: Aluna is an impersonal cosmic principle, the world of thought and consciousness preceding material reality, rather than a genealogically embedded person, so it stands apart from the family of named ancestral lords.
qemant_mezgana: Mezgana is the transcendent, uncreated supreme being of the Qemant, standing alone above all lesser spirits with no attested consort, parents, or divine kin.
even_hinken: Hinken, the god of hunting and game-luck on the sixth heaven, is attested as an individuated deity through his function and his shadow falling on the clan totem-animals, but the Even sources record no genealogy or named divine kin tying him to the other gods.
tuvaluan_foilape: Foilape is recorded only as one of the principal pre-Christian gods of the Ellice Islands, a king and famed warrior with his own shrines, without any attested genealogy or named kin in the surviving ethnographic record.
tuvaluan_telematua: Telematua is the apical founding ancestor of Funafuti and Vaitupu, standing at the head of the island genealogies with no attested parents and no kin among the other figures in this set, his wives Futi and Tupu not being independently individuated divine figures here.
tlapanec_akuniya: Akuniya is attested only as the water deity dwelling alone in the La Ciénaga marsh, the focus of localized rain-and-fertility offerings, and is not linked by the sources into the riverbank genealogy of the Sun, the Moon and the Fire god.
lenca_icelaca: Icelaca, the lord of time, is attested as an independent member of the small Lenca pantheon with no recorded kinship or marital tie to the creator pair, standing third in rank after the Great Father and Great Mother.
lenca_comizahual: Comizahual is a euhemerized human culture-heroine of the Cerquín legend rather than a member of the divine genealogy; the chronicles give her sons but name no divine parent, spouse, or sibling within the pantheon, and her link to the creator gods is cultic (she is said to have founded their worship) rather than familial.
aksumite_astar: Astar stands at the genealogical apex of the Aksumite pantheon as the celestial head-god from whom Mahrem and Beher descend; no parent or symmetric peer is attested for him, his ties to other figures being those of progenitor and of the deity to whom Hawbas is paired.
nanai_podya: The fire-spirit Podʹa (Fadzya Mama) is the indwelling numen of the household hearth, propitiated in domestic ritual rather than placed in any attested kinship or marriage with the other Nanai spirits.
nanai_duente_edeni: Duente Edeni is the master-owner of the taiga and its game, one of the parallel 'masters' of the world-zones, for whom the ethnographic sources record no kin-tie or marriage to the other figures.
nanai_temu: Temu (Mue Edeni) is the master-owner of the water world, co-ordinate with but not kin to the masters of taiga and earth; the sources attest his cult, not any genealogy or partnership.
qiang_folk_religion_shan_wang: Shan Wang is a localized village mountain-god of the white-stone pantheon, attested without genealogy or kin ties; each zhaizi keeps its own, and no marriage or descent is recorded for him (Graham 1958; Yu 2004).
qiang_folk_religion_goddess_of_the_mount: The Goddess of the Mountains is attested only as one of the five great gods embodied in the household white stones, with no recorded parentage, spouse, or other named kin in the sources (Graham 1958; Li Xianglin 2012).
qiang_folk_religion_mubyasei: Mubyasei, deified as Aba Mubita and also called Abba Chi, is the overarching God of Heaven in Qiang folk religion and the foremost of the five great gods whose white quartz stones crown every house and watchtower.
swazi_mvelinqangi: Mvelinqangi, also Mkhulumnqande ('the great-great one'), is the remote high god of the Swazi (emaSwati), a Nguni people of Eswatini.
swazi_nomkhubulwane: Nomkhubulwane, the 'Princess of the Sky' (Inkosazana), is a pan-Nguni rain-and-grain goddess associated with fertility and the first-fruits; among the Swazi her rites were performed by young women at planting time.
roman_mithraic_mysteries_arimanius: The leontocephaline (lion-headed god), attested on altars as 'deus Arimanius', is the most debated Mithraic figure: a being of time and cosmic dominion, variously identified by scholars with Aion, Kronos-Saturn, or a principle of ordered power within the mysteries.
cora_tayau: Tayau ('Our Father') is the Sun, the supreme deity of the Cora (Náayeri) of the Sierra del Nayar in Nayarit, Mexico, recorded in detail by Preuss.
cora_tetewan: Tetewan (also Hurima, Nasisa) is the Cora goddess of the moon, of rain and of the underworld of the dead, paired in opposition to the celestial sun-father Tayau in the dualistic Cora cosmos.
cora_hatsikan: Hatsikan ('Our Elder Brother'), identified with the morning star and with the maize/flower-picker god Sautari, is the Cora culture-hero and warrior who mediates between the celestial and chthonic powers; in the mitote he is the elder-brother of the deer-and-maize complex.
lega_kalaga: Among the Lega (Warega) of the Maniema forest of the eastern Congo, the divine is approached through named attributes voiced in the proverbs and objects of the Bwami initiation society.
lega_kenkunga: Kenkunga, 'the Reassembler', is a name of the divine in Lega Bwami philosophy, expressing the power that gathers and restores order out of dispersal.
lega_ombe: Ombe, 'the Hidden One', names the unsearchable, concealed dimension of the divine in Lega thought, taught in the secret grades of Bwami.
lega_kaginga: Kaginga is the incarnation of evil in Lega cosmology, the disordering power that helps witches and sorcerers; the moral instruction and solidarity of Bwami are framed as the counterweight to him.
old_prussian_occopirmus: Occopirmus ('the first', from Baltic *ūka- 'first' + pirmas 'first') is named as the foremost god, of sky and stars, in the Sudovian Book and Grunau; he heads the enumeration of the Prussian gods.
old_prussian_curche: Curche (Kurke) is the earliest historically attested Old Prussian deity, named in the Treaty of Christburg (1249) in which the converted Prussians swore to abandon his cult; he is a harvest god embodied in an idol made from the last grain of the field.
sora_kittung: Kittung is the high creator god of the Sora, a Munda (Austroasiatic) people of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh studied by Elwin and Vitebsky.
sora_labosum: Labosum, explicitly named by Elwin as the Earth-God, is the sonum of the ground; offerings are made to her for the fertility of the swiddens.
sora_uyungsum: The Sun-sonum (Uyungsum) is among the most important Sora deities, the all-seeing witness invoked in oaths and honoured with buffalo sacrifice.
sora_idital: The idital is both a guardian ancestor-sonum and the famous Sora ritual wall-painting that houses it; the ittalmaran (icon-specialist) makes the painting to settle the dead and protect the living.
wik_mungkan_taipan: Taipan is the great ancestral snake-being (pulwaiya) of the Wik-Mungkan of western Cape York Peninsula, recorded by Ursula McConnel.
wik_mungkan_bonefish: Bonefish is the pulwaiya of McConnel's 'Bonefish and Bullroarer totems', an ancestral being tied to the sacred bullroarer and the auwa increase-sites of Wik-Mungkan country.
wallisian_futunan_tagaloa: Tagaloa (Tangaloa) is the pan-Polynesian sky-creator as received on 'Uvea (Wallis) and Futuna, recorded by Burrows: the god of the heavens who orders creation and from whom the chiefly families trace descent.
wallisian_futunan_fakavelikele: Fakavelikele is named in Burrows's Ethnology of Futuna among the principal pre-Christian gods of the island, invoked for warfare and for rain.
wallisian_futunan_mafuike: Mafuike (Mafui'e) is the keeper of subterranean fire in West Polynesian myth; on Futuna and 'Uvea fire is obtained when the hero descends to Mafuike and takes it, the local form of the widespread Maui fire-theft.
wallisian_futunan_sina: Sina (Hina) is the widespread Polynesian ancestral woman; in the Futuna and 'Uvea repertoire recorded by Burrows she is heroine of the eel-and-coconut origin and of the Tinilau (Sinilau) cycle.
bon_gekho: Gekhö is the tutelary mountain god of Zhang-zhung with his own 360-deity cycle, and the scholarship (Karmay 1998; Bellezza 2008) records no attested genealogy linking him to the Four Transcendent Lords.
kapon_pia: Attested as the twin brother of the already-catalogued creator Makonaima (Roth 1915; Brett 1880); the twin bond is recorded in prose because no directed genealogical claim beyond the fraternity is documented.
kapon_piaima: Piai'ma is documented as an unattached primordial ogre and master of shamanic power with no recorded genealogy in Kapon narrative (Butt 1977; Whitehead 2002).
kapon_abel: Abel was a historical Akawaio prophet whose parentage and kin are not recorded in the ethnographic literature (Butt Colson 1960).
levantine_ditanu: Ditanu is a remote clan eponym invoked as head of the collective Rapiuma; the sources attest no individual parent, consort, or child, only a general dynastic descent claimed by the kings of Ugarit (Pardee, Ritual and Cult at Ugarit, 2002).
noongar_yondock: Yondock appears in Whadjuk narrative solely as the intruding crocodile adversary killed by the Waugal, with no attested kin (Walley, 'Origin of Derbal Nara'; City of Fremantle, 'Statements of Significance for the Fremantle Area — Whadjuk Nyoongar', 2016).
noongar_charnok_woman: The Charnok Woman travels alone gathering unnamed spirit children, with no genealogy or named divine kin recorded (Nannup, 'Moondang-ak Kaaradjiny: The Carers of Everything', 2008).
noongar_mulka: Mulka's parents are unnamed in the recorded legend, and he interacts with no other named figure of the tradition (Gunn, Records of the Western Australian Museum 23, 2006).
worrorra_namarali: Namarali is attested as the paramount Worrorra Wanjina without recorded parentage or individual kin ties; sources describe his Dreaming battle and resting place at Langgi rather than genealogy (Blundell & Woolagoodja 2005; Crawford 1968).
crow_red_woman: Red Woman appears in Crow narrative without recorded parentage or kin, acting alone as the murderous ogress of the hero cycles (Lowie, Myths and Traditions of the Crow Indians, 1918).
elema_oa_laea: Oa-Laea is the sole named protagonist of his own clan myth; no genealogical or relational ties to other named Elema figures are recorded in Brown's 1977 and 1988 editions of the myth.
elema_meavea_kivovia: Meavea Kivovia stands alone as the named ancestor of his own Eastern Elema clan tradition; the published sources (Brown 1975, 1988; Miva 1978) record no attested kinship links to other named Elema figures.
miwok_kelok: Merriam calls Ke'-lok a kinsman of Wek'-wek, but no parentage is explicitly recorded and his slayer relation runs from the existing Falcon toward him, so no outgoing links are attested (Merriam, The Dawn of the World, 1910).
miwok_chehalumche: Che-ha-lum'-che appears only as a solitary cave-dwelling ogre with no recorded kin or divine relations (Merriam, The Dawn of the World, 1910).
miwok_yayali: Yayali is a lone wandering giant; his forced marriage is to the unnamed Chipmunk's widow, and no genealogical ties are recorded (Gifford, Miwok Myths, 1917).
miwok_usumate: Her attested relations (sister-in-law Deer, the fawns) are to figures not individuated enough for the corpus, leaving her without registry links (Merriam, The Dawn of the World, 1910).
mountain_ok_magalim: Jorgensen (1998) stresses that Magalim has no origin story and stands outside Afek's ancestral genealogy, defining the wild precisely by his lack of kinship with the ancestress and her line.
mountain_ok_yomnok: Yomnok is Afek's sibling in Bimin-Kuskusmin myth (Poole 1981), but as sibling is a symmetric relation it cannot be pointed at the pre-existing Afek record, so the kinship is documented in the figure's prose and sources instead.
salish_fox: Fox travels as Coyote's elder brother and reviver in Interior Salish narratives (Teit 1912), but no parentage is attested and the only directed relation kinds available do not describe a fraternal bond to an existing corpus figure, so he stands without formal graph links.
salish_scomalt: Scomalt rules the primordial island of giants alone in the Okanagan flood narrative, with no attested parentage or ties to other named figures (Clark 1953; Erdoes & Ortiz 1984).
salish_xals: Xá:ls's attested parents (Red-Headed Woodpecker and Black Bear) are not individuated corpus figures, and the sources link him to no existing registry figure (Carlson 2001; Hill-Tout 1978).
salish_dohkwibuhch: Dohkwibuhch is the self-existent creator of the Snohomish account with no genealogy or documented relation to other named Salish figures (Clark 1953; Haeberlin & Gunther 1930).
celtiberian_airon: The epigraphic record for Airon consists of the isolated Fuente Redonda dedication and folkloric survivals, with no attested genealogy or divine partners (Lorrio & Sánchez de Prado 2002).
celtiberian_dercetius: Dercetius is known only from a single votive altar and the mountain name in the Vita Sancti Aemiliani, with no attested family or companion deities (Marco Simón 2005).
cheyenne_falling_star: Grinnell's recorded cycle (By Cheyenne Campfires, 1926) names his parents only as an unnamed star and an unnamed Cheyenne woman, giving him no attested genealogical or directed link to any registered figure.
cora_maize_girl: The myth recorded by Preuss (1912) and Benciolini (2018) places the maize girl as a bride given into a human household, not as a genealogical member of the solar pantheon of Tayau, Tetewan and Hatsikan, so no attested divine parentage or directed relation can be cited.
dacian_gebeleizis: Herodotus (Histories 4.94) is the sole ancient witness and records no genealogy for Gebeleizis; the reported identification with Zalmoxis is a contested name-equation (Eliade 1972), not an attested kinship or hierarchical relation, so the figure stands alone in the graph with the equation documented in prose.
dayak_sangumang: Sangumang appears in the recorded Ngaju folktale cycle as an upperworld trickster whose kin (his mother and his uncle the king) are never named as individuated mythological figures, so no attested genealogical links to other registry figures exist (Klokke-Coster, Klokke and Saha, De slimme en de domme, 1976).
ga_ashiakle: Ashiakle's only documented tie is filiation to the sea god Nai, recorded through her parentage (Lynch, African Mythology A to Z, 2004); no other attested relations exist.
ifugao_liddum: Ifugao ritual invocations place Liddum in the Skyworld as chief mediator without recording an attested genealogy for him (Barton, The Religion of the Ifugaos, 1946).
ifugao_ampual: Ampual is documented as a god of the Fourth Skyworld who bestows animals and plants, but the sources record no parentage or individual kin ties (Jocano, Outline of Philippine Mythology, 1969).
ifugao_namtogan: The Namtogan bulul-origin myth names no divine kin; his mortal wife at Ahin is unnamed in the recorded versions (Dulawan, Ifugao Culture and History, 2001).
jukun_kenjo: Kenjo is documented by Meek (1931) as an independent household cult-deity of war with no recorded genealogy or divine kin.
jukun_akwa: Akwa is documented by Meek (1931) as a household ancestral cult-deity with no attested genealogical ties to other named Jukun gods.
kamilaroi_mullian: Parker (1896) and Fuller et al. (2014) record Mullian's tree-burning and stellar ascent but no attested genealogy or named divine kin.
kamilaroi_wahn: Wahn appears in Parker (1896) as an independent trickster crow; the early sources give him no attested parentage or fixed relationships to other named beings.
kamilaroi_gawarrgay: Gawarrgay is a solitary celestial spirit emu in Fuller et al. (2014); the sources record no kinship ties to other named figures.
karelian_antero_vipunen: The runes present Vipunen as an isolated primeval giant lying alone in the earth, with no genealogy or kin recorded in any variant (Kuusi, Bosley & Branch, Finnish Folk Poetry: Epic, 1977).
karelian_syojatar: Syöjätär appears in charms and tales as a self-standing primordial ogress; the tradition names her unnamed tale-daughters but records no attested divine kin (Haavio, Suomalainen mytologia, 1967).
karelian_hiisi: Hiisi is the personification of the sacred grove itself and stands outside any recorded genealogy in the charm and rune corpus (Oinas, Studies in Finnic Folklore, 1985).
khoekhoe_ga_gorib: Attested solely as the pit-dwelling adversary destroyed in the Heitsi-eibib hero cycle; the tales record no kin, consort or cult for him (Bleek, Reynard the Fox in South Africa, 1864; Hahn, Tsuni-ǁGoam, 1881).
kongo_kalunga: Kalunga is attested as an impersonal cosmic ocean-force and threshold between the worlds, with no recorded genealogy or personal relations (MacGaffey, Religion and Society in Central Africa, 1986; Fu-Kiau, African Cosmology of the Bântu-Kôngo, 2001).
kongo_mbumba_luangu: Mbumba Luangu is documented as a great nature spirit (nkisi si) of the Vili and Yombe, venerated through the Khimba society without any recorded kinship to other named divinities (Bittremieux, La société secrète des Bakhimba au Mayombe, 1936; Hersak, Africa 71(4), 2001).
krachi_owuo: The Krachi origin-of-death tale presents Owuo as an isolated giant encountered on the Salaga road, with no genealogy or kinship to Wulbari, Dente, or any other Krachi figure recorded by Cardinall (Tales Told in Togoland, 1931) or Abrahamsson (The Origin of Death, 1951).
kulin_karakarook: The fire-keeper of the Pleiades appears in the recorded Kulin fire and star myths without any stated genealogy or partnerships; the crow's theft of her fire is her only narrative tie (Smyth 1878, vol. 1, pp. 458-459).
kulin_looern: William Thomas's record and later Boonwurrung tradition present Loo-errn as a self-standing guardian creator of the Western Port country, with no recorded kin ties to Bunjil, Waang or other Kulin beings (Smyth 1878, vol. 1, p. 453; Howitt 1904).
kulin_karween: Karween is attested solely as the jealous rival whom Bunjil wounded and changed into the crane, with no recorded parentage or alliances in the Woiwurrung account (Smyth 1878, vol. 1).
mende_gongoli: Gongoli stands deliberately outside the Poro and Sande hierarchies as the least sacred, unaffiliated clown of Mende masquerade, with no attested genealogical or cultic tie to other named spirits (Anderson, 'Letting the Mask Slip', Africa 88(4), 2018; Siegmann & Perani, African Arts 9(3), 1976).
mossi_oubri: Oubri carries attested parentage through Naaba Zoungrana (parent link) and needs no further relations; the genealogies (Izard 1970; Skinner 1964) individuate him solely as Zoungrana's son and dynastic founder.
nivkh_kurn: Shternberg (1933) describes Kurŋ as a singular supreme being fused with the universe itself, with no recorded parentage, consort, or offspring in Nivkh tradition.
nivkh_tugrs_ytik: Kreinovich (1973) and Ostrovsky (1997) document the Fire Grandmother as a self-standing hearth mistress with no attested kinship ties to other Nivkh masters.
shipibo_oshe: The Shipibo moon-origin myth names no divine kin for Oshe: he is a human youth whose unnamed sister marks him with huito dye before his ascent to the sky (Margery Peña 1998), so no attested genealogical or directed link to other registered figures can be drawn.
shipibo_cori_inca: Cori Inca's pairing with Yoashico Inca is a narrative opposition of hero and anti-hero rather than an attested kinship or hierarchical bond (Bertrand-Rousseau 1984), and no genealogy for him is recorded in the ethnographic literature.
swazi_somhlolo: Somhlolo is venerated as an individual royal ancestor of the Dlamini dynasty; the ethnographic record (Kuper 1947; Matsebula 1972) attests no genealogical or mythic link between him and the named divinities Mvelinqangi, Mlentengamunye, or Nomkhubulwane, whom Swazi religion keeps distinctly apart from the ancestor cult.
tibetan_buddhist_begtse: Begtse has no attested divine genealogy; his documented links (personal protector of the Third Dalai Lama, paired in cult with Palden Lhamo as the srung ma dmar nag) are historical-cultic pairings rather than kinship or hierarchy (Heller 1992; Nebesky-Wojkowitz 1956).
tibetan_buddhist_tsiu_marpo: Tsiu Marpo stands at the head of his own band of seven btsan riders with no attested parentage; his connection to Pehar is one of historical succession as protector of Samye, not a genealogical or subordination relation attested in the sources (Bell 2006; Nebesky-Wojkowitz 1956).
tibetan_buddhist_tashi_tseringma: Tseringma leads her four goddess-sisters, who are not individually authored here, and the sources record no parentage for her; her documented ties are to the human yogin Milarepa who bound her by oath (Nebesky-Wojkowitz 1956; Chang 1962).
tibetan_buddhist_dorje_shugden: Shugden's origin tradition ties him to the human lama Drakpa Gyaltsen rather than to any divine genealogy, and the sources record no kinship with other corpus deities (Dreyfus 1998; Nebesky-Wojkowitz 1956).
totonac_kiwikgolo: Ethnographies describe Kiwikgolo as a solitary Owner of the forest with no attested genealogy or divine kin (Ellison 2004; Beaucage and Rojas Mora 2022).
trobriand_topileta: Topileta appears in Malinowski's 'Baloma' (1916) as the guardian headman of the villages of the dead on Tuma with no recorded genealogy or named kin ties to other individuated Trobriand figures.
trobriand_dokonikan: Dokonikan appears in the Tudava cycle (Malinowski, Myth in Primitive Psychology, 1926) solely as the man-eating ogre slain by Tudava, with no recorded parentage or kin; the slaying is attested from Tudava's side and no directed relation runs from the ogre himself.
trobriand_inuvaylau: The legend of Inuvayla'u (Malinowski, The Sexual Life of Savages, 1929) names no individuated kin for him beyond his unnamed mother, so he stands without genealogical links in the recorded corpus.
venetic_altno: No genealogy or divine relations are attested for Altno-; he is known solely as the eponymous titular god of the Altino sanctuary in Venetic votive inscriptions (Marinetti 2009, 'Da Altno- a Giove. I. La fase preromana').
venetic_aponus: Aponus is attested only as the isolated god of the Euganean thermal springs, with no recorded kin or connections to other Venetic deities (Lazzaro 1981, Fons Aponi: Abano e Montegrotto nell'antichità).
veps_jumou: The supreme sky god Jumou stands apart from the lower mythology of host spirits; Veps sources record no genealogy or spirit-family ties for him (Vinokurova, Mifologiya vepsov: entsiklopediya, 2015).
aramean_sahar: Aramaic sources give Sahar no genealogy; the Nerab stelae (KAI 225–226) invoke him only alongside Nikkal, Nusku and Shamash as curse guarantors, without kinship statements (Gibson, Textbook of Syrian Semitic Inscriptions 2, 1975).
aramean_shamash: The Sam'alian, Sefire and Nerab inscriptions list Šamš within god-lists and curse formulae but record no parentage or consort for him in Aramaic tradition (Niehr, The Aramaeans in Ancient Syria, 2014).
aramean_iluwer: Iluwer is attested solely as the divine patron of King Zakkur of Hamath on the Tell Afis stele (KAI 202), with no genealogical or marital ties recorded (Lipiński, The Aramaeans, 2000).
arrernte_karora: Strehlow's Ilbalintja narrative (Aranda Traditions, 1947) presents Karora as a self-existing sleeping creator with no attested divine parents or documented relations to other named Arrernte figures; his sons are unnamed in the sources.
arrernte_ntjikantja_brothers: The Ntjikantja brothers appear in Strehlow's Southern Aranda material (Aranda Traditions, 1947; Songs of Central Australia, 1971) as a self-contained pair with no attested genealogical or narrative link to other named Arrernte figures.
arrernte_twanyirika: Spencer and Gillen (1899, 1927) record Twanyirika solely as the spirit of the initiation bullroarer, with no genealogy or relations to other named beings attested in the ethnography.
arrernte_yeperenye_ancestors: The caterpillar beings of Mparntwe are documented (Brooks 1991; Spencer and Gillen 1899) as an autonomous Dreaming with no attested kinship or narrative ties to other named Arrernte figures in the corpus.
bhil_rani_kajal: Rani Kajal is documented as an independent mother and clan goddess with her own hill temple near Mathvad and her own role in the Gayana creation song, without securely attested genealogical ties to the other corpus deities (Baviskar 1995).
bhil_bhilat_dev: Bhilat Dev's recorded legend makes him the son of a Gaoli herdswoman by the pan-Indian god Mahadeo, figures outside the Bhil corpus, and no kinship with the other registered Bhil deities is attested (Russell and Hira Lal 1916).
bhil_salabai: Salabai arrived among the Bhils as an external visiting goddess of the 1922-23 Devi movement and is not linked by kinship or cult to the other deities of the Bhil pantheon (Hardiman 1987).
bunun_kaipis_firebird: The kaipis acts alone in the deluge narrative as the successful fire-bringer, with no attested kinship or partnership ties to other mythic figures (Ho 1971; Ogawa & Asai 1935).
bunun_fire_toad: The toad is an independent volunteer in the fire-quest episode of the deluge myth, with no attested kinship or alliance to other figures (Ho 1971; Ogawa & Asai 1935).
cantabrian_cabuniaeginus: The single Monte Cildá altar records no genealogy or divine associations for Cabuniaeginus, an otherwise unparalleled local theonym (Iglesias Gil 1976; Olivares Pedreño 2002).
cantabrian_epane: The Monte Bernorio attestation names Epane alone, and Hispanic scholarship records no attested kinship or cult partners for this local form of the horse goddess (Peralta Labrador 2003).
cantabrian_salus_umeritana: The Otañes patera is the only testimony to Salus Umeritana and depicts her alone at her spring, with no attested genealogy or divine consorts (Iglesias Gil 2014; García y Bellido 1949).
cantabrian_nimmedus_aseddiagus: The Ujo altar is the sole attestation of Nimmedus Aseddiagus and records no relationships with other divinities (Diego Santos 1959; Marco Simón 2005).
cantabrian_vagodonnaegus: The La Milla del Río altars attest only the god's name and his civic cult, with no genealogical or mythological connections recorded (Diego Santos 1986; Olivares Pedreño 2002).
chamorro_gadao: Gadao's legends pair him only with an unnamed or inconsistently named rival chief of Tumon (Malaguana or Mataquana in different retellings), so no securely attested kin or named counterpart can be linked ("Folktale: Gådao's Strength," Guampedia).
chamorro_sirena: All recorded tellings leave Sirena's mother and godmother anonymous, so the mermaid stands without named kin (Van Peenen, Chamorro Legends on the Island of Guam, 1945; "Folktale: Sirena," Guampedia).
chamorro_anufat: Anufat is named individually among the taotaomo'na, but the sources record no genealogy or named companions for him, only his appearance and his burial-ground haunts ("Taotaomo'na," Guampedia).
chamorro_juan_malo: The Juan Malo tale cycle names no relatives or supernatural patrons for the trickster; his only steady companion is his water buffalo (Van Peenen 1945; Fee and Webb, eds., American Myths, Legends, and Tall Tales, 2016).
cree_wihtikow: The wîhtikôw stalks and hunts alone as an asocial cannibal monster, and the ethnographic record links it genealogically to no other named being (Brightman, 'The Windigo in the Material World,' Ethnohistory 35(4), 1988).
cree_pahkahkos: George Nelson's 1823 Cree material describes Pâhkahk as a lone skeletal being of starvation and disease, propitiated in feasts but tied by kinship or alliance to no other named figure (Brown and Brightman, 'The Orders of the Dreamed', 1988).
cree_cahkapes: Cahkâpês acts only alongside his unnamed elder sister, and the James Bay Cree texts attach him to no other named mythological figure (Ellis, ed., Cree Legends and Narratives from the West Coast of James Bay, 1995).
cree_ayas: Ayâs's jealous father Aioswé, his mother, and his spirit-grandmother helpers are not independently individuated in the scholarly record, so the deserted-boy hero stands alone (Skinner, Notes on the Eastern Cree and Northern Saulteaux, 1911).
diyari_marindi: Marindi appears in Diyari tradition solely as the ancestral dog slain by the gecko ancestor Adnoartina, his blood becoming the Parachilna red-ochre deposit (Horne & Aiston 1924; Howitt 1904); the sources record no parentage or other kinship for him, and the registry's directed relation kinds cannot express being slain by an existing figure.
diyari_kutji: Gason (1874) records Kutji simply as the evil being opposed to the good spirit Mooramoora and shut out of the Diyari ceremonial circle, and Howitt (1904) adds only its whirlwind form and its dealings with the medicine-men; no kinship with any muramura is recorded.
diyari_minkani: Minkani lies alone beneath his sandhill at Kudna-ngauana on the Cooper and is approached only through his increase ceremony; the legend recorded by Howitt and Siebert (1904) attaches no kinship or genealogy to him.
diyari_ngura_wordu_punnuna: His legend, recorded by Siebert and published by Howitt (1904), follows a solitary wanderer from Pando (Lake Hope) and names no kin among the other muramura of the Diyari.
enga_enda_semangko: Bulmer (1965) records no genealogy or kin ties for the Kyaka Fertility Goddess, who engages the human world only through her fertility cult.
hattic_hanwasuit: The deified throne of Hattic origin has no recorded divine kinship; Old Hittite texts pair her with the king, the regalia and the founding of the palace rather than with a divine family (Starke 1979; Haas 1994).
hattic_katahha: Kataḫḫa, 'the Queen' of Ankuwa, heads her local pantheon without securely established divine kin; a proposed tie to the Storm-god of Zippalanda, as mother or wife, remains an open question (Torri 2019).
hattic_hasamili: The divine smith and household protector has no recorded genealogy; in cult he stands among chthonic powers such as Lelwani and the fate-goddesses rather than within a divine family (Haas 1994; Taracha 2009).
hattic_teteshapi: Festival texts give this goddess of the wild her own priestess, performers and processions at Tawiniya but record no divine kinship for her (Pecchioli Daddi 1987; Klinger 1996).
hmong_nplooj_lwg: The frog creator of the Hmong Njua cosmogony stands without recorded parents, consort or divine kin; it is slain by the first, unnamed human beings (Chindarsi 1976; Tapp 1989).
hmong_xwm_kab: A domestic spirit of fortune installed at each house's main altar and renewed every New Year, recorded without genealogy or mythic kin (Chindarsi 1976; Tapp 1989).
itelmen_tuil: Krasheninnikov (Opisanie zemli Kamchatki, 1755, vol. 2, pt. 3) and Sirina & Murashko (Narody Severo-Vostoka Sibiri, 2010) record Tuil solely as the self-standing earthquake-maker who rides beneath the earth with his dog Kozei, with no kinship or subordination ties stated to any other figure.
itelmen_mitg: Krasheninnikov (Opisanie zemli Kamchatki, 1755, vol. 2, pt. 3) and Sirina & Murashko (Narody Severo-Vostoka Sibiri, 2010) describe the fish-shaped sea-master Mitg as an independent god of the sea with no recorded genealogy, consort or hierarchy.
kadazan_dusun_bisagit: Evans (1913, 1953) records Bisagit as an independent power dwelling across the primordial waters, who supplies earth to the creator couple as an outsider; no kinship with Kinoingan's divine family is anywhere attested.
kadazan_dusun_monsopiad: Oral tradition names his human parents Dunggou and Kizabon, villagers of Kuai with no further mythological identity, and connects the warrior genealogically to no figure of the divine pantheon (Gingging 2007; Phelan 2001).
kadazan_dusun_aki_nabalu: The ancestral guardian of Mount Kinabalu is venerated as the collective 'grandfather' of the dead rather than as kin or subordinate of the creator deities, and the ethnographies record no genealogical tie (Rutter 1929; Bidder 2023).
kadazan_dusun_gayo_nakan: The legend of the giant king who had himself buried in the rock at Kinabalu's foot names no parents, consort, or divine kin for him (Bidder, Kibat & Saien 2014).
kiwai_abere: The wild woman Abere acts alone in the Kiwai tales, no kinship or partnership with the other named mythical beings of the tradition being recorded for her (Landtman, The Folk-Tales of the Kiwai Papuans, 1917; Knappert, Pacific Mythology, 1992).
kiwai_ganumi: The moon-being Ganumi stands outside the genealogies of the Kiwai mythical beings; the sources personify him as the moon itself without recording parents, spouse or ties to the other named figures (Landtman, The Folk-Tales of the Kiwai Papuans, 1917).
lega_kimbilikiti: Kimbilikiti is documented as the self-contained patron spirit of the Lega bwálí circumcision complex, with no genealogy or attested narrative tie linking him to the Lega creator divinity's epithet cycle or to other named figures (Masumbuko Wa-Busungu, Grammaire du kilega/lega, 2019; Vogel, L'Afrique des Grands Lacs: Annuaire 2013-2014, 2014).
lenca_entepica: Herrera's chronicle individuates Entepica solely as the paramount lord of Cerquín and Piraera who entrusted the war against the Spaniards to Lempira; no kin, consort, or divine ties are attested for him (Herrera, Historia general, Década VI, 1601–1615; Chapman, Los lencas de Honduras en el siglo XVI, 1978).
mandan_old_woman_who_never_dies: Maximilian (1843) and Bowers (1950) record the corn goddess as an independent divinity honored at the women's corn-medicine feasts and by the Goose Society, with no genealogical or kinship ties to the Mandan creator figures.
mbuti_kalisia: Attested as the gracious lord of the forest and its game with a hunters' offering-hut cult but no recorded kin, consort or offspring (Roome, Apolo: The Apostle to the Pygmies, 1934; Zuesse, Ritual Cosmos, 1979; Jordan, Encyclopedia of Gods, 1993); Epulu usage equates the name with the forest divinity itself rather than placing it in any genealogy.
mbuti_masupa: Schebesta's Efe narrative introduces Masupa as 'quite alone, with neither wife nor brother', and his three children — the ancestors of the peoples — remain unnamed, so no named kin edge is attestable (Revisiting My Pygmy Hosts, 1936).
vanuatu_ro_som: Ro Som, the money-spirit of Mota, appears in Codrington's ethnography (The Melanesians, 1891, ch. xix) only in her dealings with the mortal Ganviviris and has no recorded kinship or mythological tie to any other named figure of the tradition.
vanuatu_lehevhev: Le-hev-hev, the devouring Guardian Ghost of Malekula (Layard, Stone Men of Malekula, 1942), stands outside any recorded genealogy; the sources attach her to the journey of the dead and the tusked-boar sacrifices of the Maki rather than to other named mythological persons.
nupe_ndaduma: Sources record the worship of Ndaduma, the personified 'Father Niger', at Gbara and Jima as an independent river divinity, without genealogical or cultic ties to other named Nupe powers (Sidi 2015; Salihu 2022).
oromo_akkoo_manooyyee: Oral tradition individuates Akkoo Manooyyee as the queen of the pre-gadaa era of women's rule without recording any divine parentage or kinship linking her to other figures of the tradition (Imana, 'Some Notes on the Past of Oromo Society: The Story about Akkoo Manooyyee in Focus,' East African Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities 8/1, 2023).
otomi_muye: Colonial and modern sources record Muye only as the Otomi rain lord equated with Tlaloc, preserving no native genealogy or kin ties for him (Wright Carr 2007; Méndez Gómez 2023, Cuicuilco 30(88)).
otomi_edahi: The Relación geográfica de Querétaro (1582, ed. Acuña 1987) presents Eday as a self-standing creator and wind god of the Jilotepec Otomi, recording no family or consorts (cf. Carrasco 1950; Wright Carr 2007).
otomi_acpaxapo: The Anales de Cuauhtitlan (tr. Bierhorst 1992) attest Acpaxapo solely as the oracle-serpent of Lake Xaltocan who prophesied in wartime, with no kinship to other Otomi gods recorded (Carrasco 1950).
otomi_maka_xumpo_dehe: Sierra Otomi ethnography lists the Lady of the Waters as an independent owner-mistress of springs among the principal deities, without stated genealogy (Dow ed. 1995, Encyclopedia of World Cultures vol. 8; Galinier 2004).
otomi_maka_hai: Dow's ethnographic account of the Sierra Otomi pantheon names Lord Earth as an independent approachable deity with no recorded kin relations (Dow ed. 1995; Galinier 2004).
pomo_kilak: Barrett's Pomo Myths (1933) and the Central Pomo monster-bird dance record the kilak as an independent monster-bird without attested genealogy or fixed kinship ties to other Pomo mythic figures.
rarotongan_tutapu: The traditions individuate Tutapu wholly through his feud with the founder Tangiia; the sources record for him no divine parentage, no consort and no line of descendants, his mother Maonga and foster father Pou-vananga-roa being bare genealogical names (S. Percy Smith, Hawaiki, 1910; Te Ariki-tara-are, JPS 28-29, 1919-1920).
ryukyuan_hinukan: The hearth deity is worshipped in each household without any recorded parentage or kinship in the ethnographic literature, serving instead as intermediary between the family and the gods of heaven (Lebra, Okinawan Religion, 1966).
ryukyuan_tentei: The Heavenly Emperor stands at the apex of the Ryukyuan creation account with no recorded parentage or kinship of his own; the chronicles record only the commands he issues to the deities he sends down, who are registered here as his subordinates (Chūzan Seikan, 1650).
ryukyuan_miruku: A visiting god who comes to the islands from the sea-otherworld Nirai Kanai; the sources record festival visitation and blessing rather than any genealogical or kinship tie (Ouwehand, Hateruma, 1985).
semang_begjag: Begjag is recorded only as a grandchild of the grandmother goddess Yak Manoid, in the same divine generation as Kaei (Karei) and Ta Ped'n, and the sources name no parents, consort, or other individual ties for this figure (Evans 1937, ch. XIV).
semang_ag_ag: Ag-ag the crow appears in the record solely as the progenitor of Jamoi, Jalang, and Klang, and the sources name no parentage, consort, or alliance for Ag-ag itself (Evans 1937, p. 149).
semang_tohan: Endicott (1979) presents Tohan as a solitary creator god who acts on humans directly through disease and accident, with no kinship ties to the thunder god or to any other being recorded in the sources.
sicel_sikelos: Eponymous ancestor-king of the Sicels whose attested kin in the origin legends — his father Italos in Philistus of Syracuse and his host King Morges in Antiochus (both preserved in Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 1.12.3 and 1.22.3-5) — are mainland Italic figures not registered in this tradition, leaving no in-registry bond of the allowed kinds.
sicel_leukaspis: Sican battle-hero known from Diodorus 4.23.5 and the Syracusan drachms naming him; his slayer Heracles admits no allowed inbound relation kind, and the fellow Sican generals listed with him (Pediacrates, Buphonas and others) are bare names nowhere further individuated, so no kinship of the allowed kinds can be anchored.
sicel_chrysas: Deified river of the Sikel town of Assorus attested by Cicero (Verrines 2.4.96) and the town's coinage; no genealogy, consort or divine kin of any kind is recorded for him in the ancient testimony.
sicel_meteres_of_engyon: Collective mother-goddesses of the Engyon sanctuary attested by Diodorus 4.79.5-80.6, Plutarch (Marcellus 20) and Cicero (Verrines 2.4.97); their only stated connections are to Cretan figures of Greek myth (the infant Zeus they nursed), and no source links them by kinship to the registered Sikel-Sicani figures.
somali_arraweelo: The recorded Arraweelo legend names no kin or divine partners: the wise old man who evades her and the grandson who kills her remain anonymous in the tale collections (Hanghe 1988; Mukhtar 2003, s.v. 'Araweelo').
somali_dhegdheer: Recorded tellings of the Dhegdheer tale give the ogress no named kin — her daughter and her victims are anonymous — and she stands apart from the Waaq pantheon as a free-standing cautionary figure (Hassan 2007; Lilius, Bildhaan).
sora_jalia: Thurston (1909), quoting Fawcett (1888), records Jalia as a masterless wandering deity moving from village to village, with no kinship or hierarchy linking it to other Sora powers.
sora_rattud: Vitebsky (1993) treats Ra'tud as a self-contained collective sonum category parallel to, but not genealogically connected with, the Sun and Earth categories.
sora_jodisum: Patel (2005) and INTACH (2018) record Jodisum only as the free-standing village deity of the crossroads, with no attested genealogy or hierarchy among the Sora sonums.
sora_manduasum: INTACH (2018) and the Odisha State Tribal Museum documentation record Manduasum as an independent village-protecting deity with its own shrine and no recorded kinship to other Sora deities.
thai_lao_mae_khongkha: Anuman Rajadhon (Loy Krathong & Songkran Festival, 1956) records her cult as an independent veneration of the personified 'Mother of Waters' at the floating-lights rites, and Thai-Lao sources give her no parentage or consort among the tradition's other figures.
thai_lao_phaya_khankhak: In the Isan epic (Wajuppa Tossa, Phya Khankhaak, the Toad King, 1996) the Toad King is born to a human royal house and meets the sky lord Thaen only as a battlefield adversary, so no genealogical link to the tradition's other figures is attested.
thai_lao_thao_hung_cheuang: Chamberlain (Mon-Khmer Studies 18–19, 1989–1990) presents Thao Hung/Cheuang as a hero of purely human royal descent in the pre-Buddhist Tai epic, with no attested kinship to the tradition's divine figures.
tlingit_hayicanak: The recorded cosmology gives the earth-supporting old woman no kin: she stands alone beneath the world-post, harassed but never displaced by Raven in Krause's account (Krause 1956 [1885]; Swanton 1909).
