tlingit_gonakadet: Swanton's Wrangell narrative derives the Gonakadet from an unnamed human hunter, and his wife and daughters became the unnamed collective creek-women rather than individuated figures, leaving no citable genealogical tie to any registry figure (Swanton 1909).
tlingit_tlanaxeedakw: Ethnographies describe the Wealth Woman as a solitary forest apparition carrying a nameless infant and record no kinship between her and any other individuated Tlingit being (de Laguna 1972; McClellan 1963).
tlingit_natsilane: The killer-whale maker acts alone in clan tradition; his brothers-in-law and the whales he carved remain unnamed in the sources, so no attested relation to another registered figure exists (Swanton 1909; Dauenhauer and Dauenhauer 1987).
tlingit_duktootl: The Strong Man's uncle, kinsfolk, and the sea lions of his feat are unnamed in the recorded versions, leaving Blackskin without documented links to other individuated figures (Swanton 1909; Dauenhauer and Dauenhauer 1987).
tlingit_kaats: Kaats''s bear wife and bear children are unnamed in the recorded tellings, so no cited relation to another individuated figure can be registered (Swanton 1909; Dauenhauer and Dauenhauer 1987).
toraja_pong_lalondong: Attested across the scholarship as the cock-lord who rules, guards and judges the dead in Puya, but with no parentage or marriage recorded for him in the liturgical god-genealogies (Nooy-Palm, The Sa'dan-Toraja I, 1979; Van der Veen, The Sa'dan Toradja Chant for the Deceased, 1966).
toraja_indo_belo_tumbang: Named in the scholarship only as the goddess of curative medicine invoked in the maro ritual, with no genealogy or consort recorded ('Toraja Religion', The Encyclopedia of Religion, vol. 14, 1987; Nooy-Palm, The Sa'dan-Toraja II, 1986).
wayuu_ulepala: Ulepala is remembered as a solitary legendary man whose myth records no attested parentage or kin, only his lone journey to the land of the dead (Perrin 1976).
wik_mungkan_kapa: Kapa the Moon is an independent celestial pulwaiya with its own origin story and totemic site, recorded without any attested genealogical tie to other Munkan ancestors (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
wik_mungkan_min_monti: Min Monti the jabiru is a self-standing clan totem centred on its own increase-site (auwa), with no attested kinship to other pulwaiya (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
wik_mungkan_min_wuka: Min Wuka the flying-fox is an independent clan pulwaiya with its own myth and increase-site, recorded without attested genealogical links (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
wik_mungkan_kongkong: Kongkong the white fish-hawk is a self-standing totemic ancestor tied to the origin of the fishing-net and its own site, with no attested kinship to other pulwaiya (McConnel, Myths of the Munkan, 1957).
yapese_lug: Müller records Lug (Lugalang) as one of the two great Yapese sky gods beside Yalafath, but the tradition transmits him without attested parentage or named divine associates; in afterlife belief he devours the soul-that-dies together with an unnamed friend.
aymara_ekeko: Colonial and archaeological sources present Ekeko as an independent household god of abundance with no attested divine parentage, consort or sibling (Ponce Sanginés, Tunupa y Ekako, 1969).
aymara_wari: Bouysse-Cassagne describes Wari as a primordial, autochthonous chthonic power of the world below whose myths give him no attested lineage or partner (Bouysse-Cassagne, Lluvias y cenizas, 1988).
bai_li_mi: Li Mi entered Bai religion as a defeated Tang enemy general propitiated at the General's Cave, standing outside the genealogy of the Nanzhao-Dali pantheon with no attested kin or divine peers.
bai_xinuluo: Xinuluo is venerated as a self-standing founding ancestor and mountain lord of Weibaoshan whose recorded kin (father Jiadupang, grandfather Shelong) are not themselves individuated benzhu in this corpus.
berber_bonchor: Bonchor stands at the centre of the Dii Mauri relief from Vaga, but the registry does not yet contain the other six Moorish gods (Macurgum, Matilam, Vihinam, Varsissima, Macurtam, Iunam) with whom he formed that local pantheon, so no in-set relation is available (Camps 1954).
berber_aulisua: Aulisua is attested only by isolated Latin dedications naming him as deus sanctus, with no genealogy or divine associate recorded in the sources (Benabou 1976).
berber_ieru: Ieru is known solely from a single Numidian rock inscription with a radiate head, which records no kin or companion deity (Camps, Encyclopedie berbere, s.v. 'Ieru').
berber_bacax: Bacax is documented only by the dated cave dedications of Thibilis, which attach no consort, parent, or fellow deity to him (Camps, Encyclopedie berbere, vol. 9, 1991).
bicolano_bakunawa: Bakunawa is recorded in the Bicol lexicon of Marcos de Lisboa purely as the cosmic serpent that swallows the moon during eclipses, with no attested genealogical or narrative link to the Gugurang-Asuang pantheon or the Ibalong heroes.
choctaw_nalusa_chito: Choctaw sources describe Nalusa Chito / Impa Shilup as a solitary predatory shadow-being with no recorded parentage, offspring, or spouse; he acts alone upon vulnerable individuals (Swanton 1931; Mould 2004).
choctaw_bohpoli: Bohpoli / Kowi Anukasha is depicted as a small man who 'lived alone in the woods' and let himself be seen by no one, with no attested kin among the wider Choctaw pantheon (Bushnell 1909; Swanton 1931).
choctaw_hoklonoteshe: Hoklonote'she appears in the ethnographic record as an isolated shape-shifting spirit defined by its powers rather than by any family or alliance (Swanton 1931).
choctaw_ishkitini: Ishkitini is recorded as an independent night-prowling owl-being and death omen without documented genealogy or relations to other figures (Swanton 1931; Bushnell 1909).
dine_coyote: Coyote (Mąʼii / Áłtsé Hashké) is a boundary-crossing trickster whose defining role is to stand apart from and disrupt the ordered company of the Holy People rather than to be fixed in stable kinship or alliance with any one of them (Haile, Navajo Coyote Tales, 1984; Luckert, Coyoteway, 1979).
embera_ba: Ba, the Thunder, is named only as one of the beings that co-inhabit the upper world (bajía) with Karagabí, with no attested genealogy or personal relationship of its own (Bioetnia 2011).
evenki_agdy: Agdy, the personified thunder and its iron thunder-birds, is tied in Evenki belief to individual shamans and to the thunder-ancestors of the lower world rather than descended within the sky-god's lineage, and the sources document it as standing apart from the creator genealogy (Vasilevich 1969; Ol'khovatov 2023).
haida_property_woman: She is a self-standing wealth-spirit encountered in the forest and along the shore, with no genealogy or fixed partner attested in Swanton's or Barbeau's records.
haida_konankada: The Chief of the Undersea World is depicted as an independent sovereign of the sea-realm, without attested parentage or spouse in the Haida sources.
haida_nanasimgit: He is the hero of a self-contained rescue narrative whose only named relative, his wife Ḵ'uljáad, is not otherwise an individuated figure of the pantheon.
huichol_kieri: Kieri stands apart as the solitary malevolent plant-sorcerer and adversary of the deer culture-hero, not a member of the ancestral 'Our Mothers/Fathers' family, and the sources give him no attested parentage (Furst & Myerhoff 1966; Knab 1977).
huichol_haramara: Tatéi Haramara is the independent divine personification of the Pacific Ocean venerated at the western sacred site of San Blas, presented in the sources as a primeval water-mother without fixed divine parentage (Lumholtz 1900; Schaefer & Furst 1996).
huichol_niwetsika: Tatéi Niwetsika is the maize-mother whose five daughters are the coloured corn-maidens; the sources present her as an autonomous 'Our Mother' ancestor-deity of sustenance without a fixed divine parentage (Zingg 1938; Myerhoff 1974).
ijaw_bouakarakarabiri: As an independent forest wizard he stands outside the Orua lineages, dispensing invulnerability-charms to hero and rival alike rather than belonging to either family.
ket_kaigus: The forest-master Kaigus is documented as an independent owner-spirit of the taiga with no attested genealogy or myth-kinship to the cosmic deities, standing alone among the Ket masters of nature (Alekseenko 1967).
ket_kholai: Kholai is recorded only as the free-standing mistress of the hunted animals, without cited parentage or narrative ties to other Ket figures (Alekseenko 1967; Vajda 2011).
ket_ulgys: Ulgys is attested solely as the autonomous owner of the rivers and their fish, with no genealogical or relational links to the sky-god or other beings in the sources (Alekseenko 1967; Vajda 2011).
khmer_preah_pisnukar: The divine architect of the Poem of Angkor Wat acts alone as Indra's sent craftsman and has no attested kin or peer within the Khmer founder-pantheon (Jacob 1996).
khmer_preah_thorani: The Buddhist earth goddess is a self-standing cosmic witness with no attested genealogy or peer relationship in the Khmer record, defined solely by her role beneath the Buddha's throne (Guthrie 2004).
khmer_yeay_mao: As an individuated local tutelary spirit she stands as her own named cult without attested kinship or partnership to the other figures of the Khmer pantheon (Ang Choulean 1986).
kirati_nahangma: Nahangma stands apart as the martial mountaintop deity of the Nahangma rite whose one narrative tie is an antagonism with the grandmother-goddess Yuma; because that bond is a symmetric opposition with a pre-existing figure it is described in prose rather than wired, leaving her without an attested genealogical parent or directed link.
klamath_llao: Llao's defining bond is his adversarial relationship with the above-world chief Skell, expressed narratively in the Crater Lake origin story rather than through any attested kinship, parentage, or subordination tie recordable as a directed relation (Clark 1953; Deur 2008).
kondh_niyam_raja: As the supreme god-king and mythic ancestor of the Dongria Kondh sub-group, Niyam Raja heads his own Niyamgiri cosmology and is not attested with a genealogical tie to the plains-Kondh Bura Pennu pantheon.
kondh_nirantali: Nirantali is the self-standing creatrix of the distinct Kuttia Kondh cosmogony and is not documented as child, consort or subordinate of the Bura Pennu and Tari Pennu creation account.
kondh_banka_mundi: The encyclopaedic sources present Banka-Mundi as an independent Kondh hunting and fertility goddess without recording any parentage or fixed relation to the other named Pennu.
kunwinjku_nawura: Nawura is documented as an independent stone-country creator-ancestor of the escarpment around Gunbalanya, without an attested genealogy or personal tie to the other recorded Kunwinjku ancestral beings in the available sources (Nganjmirra 1997; National Gallery of Australia collection records).
lardil_nyaranbi: Attested as a co-equal totemic law-giving Dreaming ancestor beside the Rainbow Serpent Thuwathu, with no recorded genealogical kin of his own (McKnight 1999).
lardil_gidegal: Documented as an independent Moon ancestor presiding over initiation and the afterlife, without attested family ties to other Lardil ancestors (Roughsey 1971).
lardil_kaltharr: Recorded solely as the Yellow Trevally ancestor who authored the Damin ceremonial language, with no attested kin relations (Hale & Nash 1997).
lenape_snow_boy: Snow Boy is recorded as a fatherless child born to a mortal woman and stands apart from the Creator and the great manitou, with no attested divine parentage or kin (Harrington 1921; Bierhorst 1995).
luo_owiny_sigoma: He led a distinct Jok-Owiny migration wave and founded the Karuoth royal clan, a lineage Ogot treats as separate from the common eponymous descent, leaving him without an attested tie to the existing figures.
luo_gor_mahia: He is a self-standing late-eighteenth- to nineteenth-century magician-chief of Kanyamwa whose attested kin (father Ogada, grandfather Ogalo) lie outside the corpus and who bears no recorded relation to the other Luo figures.
luo_nyamgondho: He is an independent lakeshore folktale hero of the Suba/Gwassi country whose kin belong only to his own tale and who is unconnected to the Luo migration genealogy.
lycian_kakasbos: Kakasbos is an independent Anatolian rider-god of Lycia and Pisidia documented only through votive stelai, with no attested genealogy or kinship to other members of the Lycian pantheon; his sole documented linkage is a later interpretatio with Herakles.
lydian_baki: Baki (Pakiš) is attested only as an isolated theonym, priestly title and month-name in the Lydian texts, with no genealogical link to other Lydian gods recorded.
lydian_malis: Malis (Maλiš) is known chiefly from a single bilingual dedication and scattered notices, which document her identity and domains but record no kinship or partnership with other Lydian deities.
maidu_rattlesnake: Maidu tradition names Rattlesnake only as the autonomous animal-person who brings the first death by biting Coyote's son, giving him no attested parentage or kin group (Dixon, Maidu Myths, 1902).
malagasy_darafify: Darafify (Rapeto) is remembered as a solitary wandering colossus whose deeds shape the land; the recorded tales attach him to no divine genealogy, only to eponymous wives who are themselves mere personifications of the lakes Rasoabe and Rasoamasay (Renel 1910).
marind_aramemb: Stands alone as the eponymous culture-hero dema of a Marind phratry, treated by van Baal (1966) as an independent healer figure in the origin-of-death cycle rather than through fixed divine kinship.
marind_yorma: Recorded by van Baal (1966) as the personified sea-dema, son of the depth-dema Desse and Dawena, who are not themselves individuated figures in the present set.
marind_dawi: Appears in van Baal (1966) as the cassowary-dema of the origin-of-fire and island-of-Habee episode without attested genealogical ties to the other named dema.
mentawai_sikameinan: In the sources Sikameinan is a discrete local water spirit of southern Siberut invoked to enforce meat-sharing, and is not attached by genealogy or subordination to the four cosmic ruling spirits.
mentawai_pageta_sabbau: Pageta Sabbau is a self-standing culture hero and first shaman whose myth involves only his own people and no attested kinship to the ruling spirits or the high deity.
murinbata_pilirin: Pilirin the Kestrel appears in the Rainbow Serpent myth solely as the being who rescues fire when Kunmanggur takes it into the sea, and Stanner records no kin tie or ranked relation attaching him to the other ancestors.
nabataean_shai_al_qaum: He is a self-standing tutelary god of caravans and the tribe with no attested Nabataean genealogy or consort, honoured independently in his own dedications from Palmyra to Hegra.
nabataean_obodas_the_god: As a divinised king absorbed into cult, he is venerated in his own right at Oboda and Petra without an attested divine parentage or spouse in the Nabataean sources.
nabataean_ara: His individuality rests on a tutelary role at Bostra and his eventual identification with Dushara rather than on any attested genealogy or symmetric kin-tie.
nabataean_hubal: He is invoked as an independent divine guarantor in the Hegra tomb curse, standing beside Dushara and Manōtu without any attested Nabataean kinship or directed cult-subordination.
nenets_pe_mal_khada: Pe-mal Khada is documented as an autonomous tutelary goddess of the northern Ural ridge with no attested genealogy or spousal tie in the Nenets pantheon (Kharyuchi 2018; Khomich 1995).
nias_buruti_siraso: She belongs to the discrete Teteholi Ana'a agricultural-origin cycle, in which she is daughter of a heavenly king (Balugu Silaride Ana'a) not otherwise present in the corpus, and is not attested in a fixed genealogical relation to the existing Nias figures, per Mendröfa, Fondrakö Ono Niha (1981).
niuean_mataginifale: Her recorded genealogy runs through the mortal chiefly line of Malotele and Tehamau rather than the migrant tupua, and the human and divine kin named in her whale legend are not otherwise individuated in the existing corpus.
nuristani_wushum: Worshipped as a creator-god of localized observance, identified with or set above Imra rather than by fixed kinship, he stands as a parallel supreme figure without attested genealogy (Jettmar 1986; Halfmann 2022).
nuristani_krumai: The goat-goddess of Tirich Mir is defined by her mountain and her theriomorphy rather than by descent or marriage, appearing in myth as an autonomous visitor among the gods (Jettmar 1986).
nuristani_arom: A tribal tutelary deity of the Kata (Kam) attached to his shrine and holy stone at Kamdesh, recorded without parentage or divine kin (Robertson 1896).
old_prussian_bardoayts: Named only in the Sudovian Book's descending list of gods as the god of ships and seafarers, with no attested kinship or narrative tie linking him to the other Old Prussian deities.
pende_mbangu: Mbangu is a fixed named personage of the mbuya masquerade repertoire whose scholarly documentation records no attested genealogical or personal tie to the other Pende mask-spirits or high gods.
pende_tundu: Tundu functions as the independent clown-transgressor of the mbuya repertoire, documented as a stand-alone character rather than through any attested kinship or partnership with other figures.
pende_giwoyo: Giwoyo is documented as a distinct bearded mask of the honoured dead, with no attested individuated relationship to other named Pende figures in the sources consulted.
pende_gitenga: Gitenga is described only as the elder or chief of the collective minganji fibre masks, a class rather than a named individual, and the sources record no personal tie to other individuated figures.
rotuman_kirkirsasa: Kirkirsasa appears in Rotuman tradition as an independent legendary heroine of Tarkei with no attested genealogical or narrative ties to the other recorded figures of the pantheon.
selkup_ponege: The pönege is a stock man-eating forest ogre of the It'a/Icha oral tales with no attested descent from, or marriage into, the Selkup divine family; it stands outside the cosmological genealogy as the hero's monstrous adversary (Tuchkova et al. 2010; Pelikh 1998).
sinhala_folk_yakku_oddisa: Oddisa stands apart as the archetypal originating exorcist and founder of the Suniyama rite rather than a figure embedded in the demonic genealogies, per Bruce Kapferer, The Feast of the Sorcerer (1997).
tharu_daharchandi: She presides as the foremost independent goddess of the maruwa than village shrine, with no genealogical tie to the existing corpus figures attested in the ethnographic record; her only named kin, Draupadi, is an epic Hindu figure outside this tradition.
tlapanec_akuun_mbaa: Attested as an autonomous 'god of the earth' who owns the animals and gives the seeds; Me'phaa sources describe his cult and offerings without ascribing him a parent or a named divine partner.
tlapanec_akuun_juba: The 'lord of the mountain' is documented as an independent owner of wild game addressed in hunting prayer, with no attested parentage or spouse in the Me'phaa record.
toda_meilitars: Meilitars is remembered as a self-standing deified culture-hero, a mortal Toda later revered as a god for originating the calf-sacrifice, whose links to the high-god family of On and Teikirzi are not specified in the ethnographic record (Walker 1992; Rivers 1906).
urartian_selardi: Selardi appears only as a name within the Meher Kapısı sacrificial catalogue with no attested spouse, parentage, or genealogical tie to other Urartian deities.
vietnamese_thuy_tinh: He is defined wholly by his perpetual mythic rivalry with the mountain saint over Princess Mỵ Nương, an antagonism the registry has no directed link to encode toward the pre-existing mountain-god figure, and he has no attested divine parentage or named kin of his own (Nguyễn Đổng Chi, Kho tàng truyện cổ tích Việt Nam, 1957–1982).
vietnamese_mau_thoai: Her only attested kin is her father the Dragon King of Động Đình Lake, a figure not separately individuated in this corpus, and she has no other named relations among the registered figures (Ngô Đức Thịnh, Đạo Mẫu Việt Nam, 2009).
wichi_nilataj: Recorded as a remote, self-standing celestial creator who framed the world before other beings existed; the ethnographic sources give him no attested parentage and no fixed genealogical tie to the sun, moon, trickster or rainbow-serpent of the corpus.
wichi_kates: The Star Woman descends alone from among the stars to an unnamed mortal hunter, and the sources attest no divine parent or named divine partner linking her to existing figures in the corpus.
yakut_kydai_bakhsy: The smith-god is portrayed as the self-standing first blacksmith of the lower world, without an attested genealogical or marital tie to the other named deities of the pantheon.
yakut_baai_baianai: The master of the taiga is an independent hunting spirit whose worship stands on its own, with no attested kinship or consort bond to the other named Yakut deities.
yakut_aan_alakhchyn: As the indwelling mistress of the earth and world tree, she is depicted autonomously and is not given a securely attested parent, spouse, or sibling among the named pantheon figures.
zulu_uhlakanyana: As a folktale trickster born precociously to a mortal chief's wife, Uhlakanyana carries no attested genealogical or cultic link to the creator deities and stands as a self-contained legendary figure, per Callaway (1868) and Werner (1933).
tibetan_bon_welchen_gekho: As the autonomous patron mountain-god of the kingdom of Zhang-zhung and Mount Kailash, Gekhö is documented as a self-standing tutelary and meditational deity rather than as a member of an attested divine family.
